question: Which of the following parts of a plant does NOT take part in vegetative propagation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Flower**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction in plants where new plants grow from parts other than seeds.
 
• Roots, stems, and leaves can all give rise to new plants through vegetative propagation.
 
• Common examples include the propagation of plants like potatoes from tubers (stem), onions from bulbs (stem), and Bryophyllum from leaves.
 
• Flowers, however, are primarily involved in sexual reproduction and do not participate in vegetative propagation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vegetative Propagation Methods:**

 
 
• **Cutting:** Involves rooting a severed piece of the parent plant.
 
• **Layering:** Involves bending a stem to the ground and covering it with soil to encourage roots to form.
 
• **Grafting:** Involves joining two plant parts from different plants.
 
• **Tissue Culture:** Growing plants from cells in a nutrient medium.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• Ensures uniformity in plant characteristics.
 
• Faster growth and maturity compared to seed propagation.
 
• Preserves desirable traits of the parent plant.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• Lack of genetic diversity, making plants susceptible to pests and diseases.
 
• Propagation materials may carry diseases.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Vegetatively Propagated Plants:**
 
 
• Potato (tubers), Sweet Potato (roots).
 
• Strawberry (runners), Sugarcane (stem cuttings).
 
• Bryophyllum (leaves), Onion (bulbs).
